# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 27 (Bi-Vb Pc27)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Paṭibāhana Sikkhāpada* (Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 27) is an ecclesiastical rule in the Vinaya Piṭaka regulating the communal distribution of robe material among Buddhist nuns [Hüsken 1997]. According to the rule, a nun who obstructs or blocks a legitimate and appropriate distribution of robe-cloth commits an offense requiring expiation (*pācittiya*) [Hüsken 1997]. In the canonical origin narrative, the nun Thullanandā creates an obstacle to the community's acquisition of robes (*cīvaralābhaṃ antarāyaṃ akāsi*) [Hüsken 1997]. Subsequent casuistry in the commentary and analysis specifies that obstructing the receipt of other monastic requisites constitutes a lesser offense of wrongdoing (*dukkaṭa*) [Hüsken 1997]. Ute Hüsken notes that this rule has no direct parallel in the Pātimokkha rules for monks [Hüsken 1997]. It has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
